short: SF Admin. Code § 37.15 (Reporting & Rent Increase License)
title: Sec. 37.15 — Reporting Obligations; Licensing (S.F. Administrative Code Ch. 37)
quote: (a) Owners of residential dwelling units subject to this Chapter 37 shall be required to report certain information about their units to the Rent Board ... (c) For condominium units and units in buildings with fewer than 10 units, the information shall be reported commencing March 1, 2023 and updated annually by March 1 of each successive year. ... (e) If a landlord has substantially complied with the obligation to report information about a rental unit as required under this Section 37.15, the landlord shall receive a license to impose rent increases on tenants in that unit under Sections 37.3(a)(1)-(2). If the landlord has not substantially complied with the reporting obligation, then the license to impose rent increases shall be temporarily suspended during the period of the landlord's noncompliance. Upon receipt of the required information from the landlord, the suspension shall be terminated, and the license to impose rent increases shall be restored prospectively, but a tenant shall not be obligated to pay the increased rent for months during the period of suspension.
used_for: Establishes mandatory annual Housing Inventory reporting for all owners of 1–9 unit buildings (including individual 2-unit owners since March 1, 2023), license issuance upon substantial compliance, suspension during noncompliance, and prospective-only restoration.

short: SF Rent Board Housing Inventory Guide
title: The Rent Board Housing Inventory
quote: All owners of residential property are required to report. ... Reporting is free and can be done online 24/7. ... Property owners who report that a unit is tenant-occupied will receive a rent increase license that allows them to impose annual allowable and banked rent increases. ... Deadline: March 1 of every year. You can still make a Housing Inventory submission and receive a rent increase license after the deadline. However, your rent increase notice will not be enforceable without having a rent increase license on the effective date of the notice. ... The Rent Board does not assess monetary penalties for filing after the deadline. ... The information entered in the housing inventory submission is public. ... The rent increase license does not need to be included with your rent increase notice.
used_for: Confirms free 24/7 online reporting, automatic license generation for non-owner-occupied units, effective-date enforceability rule, zero monetary penalty for late filing, public disclosure, and individual-unit submission recommendation for small properties.

short: SF Rent Board Rules Part XIII (§§ 13.10–13.14 Licensing & Banking Preservation)
title: Rent Board Rules and Regulations: Part XIII — Reporting Obligations Under Rent Ordinance Section 37.15
quote: Section 13.13: an owner or manager shall not be penalized for failure to report information accurately or stating it is unknown, so long as they have reported the requested information 'to the best of the owner's or manager's knowledge.' Section 13.14: Any rent increase under Ordinance Sections 37.3(a)(1)-(2) purporting to be effective while the landlord is unlicensed shall render the entire rent increase null and void; provided, however, that the effective date of the rent increase, not the date of service, shall be used to determine whether or not the increase conforms with the provisions of this section. Nothing in this Regulation shall affect a landlord's banking rights or the ability to accumulate otherwise lawful rent increases that were found to be null and void.
used_for: Establishes the exact regulatory rule that license validity is tested on the effective date (not service date), good-faith approximation satisfies substantial compliance (§ 13.13), and an unlicensed voided notice does not forfeit underlying banking rights (§ 13.14).

short: SF Rent Board Notice of Owner Noncompliance (Tenant Summary vs. Unlawful Petitions)
title: Notice of Owner Noncompliance with Housing Inventory
quote: Check the Rent Board Portal to learn if there was a license on the effective date of your rent increase. If there was no Rent Increase License then fill out a Tenant Petition for Unlawful Rent Increase [Form 516C] to challenge the Rent Increase Notice. If the rent increase has not yet gone into effect fill out a Tenant Summary Petition [Form 518]. ... Paper filings can be emailed to rentboard.inventory@sfgov.org or dropped off at the Rent Board office between 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM.
used_for: Explains why individual owners should obtain the Rent Increase License BEFORE serving notice: tenants can search by address/APN immediately and file Form 518 (before effective date) or Form 516C (after effective date for a rent refund).

short: SF Rent Board Online Portal (portal.sfrb.org)
title: Welcome to the San Francisco Rent Board's Housing Inventory and Fee Portal
quote: The Portal is a secure database that allows users to view property information, comply with the City's Housing Inventory requirements, and pay annual Rent Board fees. Property Owners/Managers: Submit information about your units to comply with the City's Housing Inventory requirements; Obtain a License to increase rents for tenants covered by Rent Control ... Tenants: View status of landlord's current License to increase rent for a unit.
used_for: Official City portal URL for creating an owner account, submitting Housing Inventory unit reports, paying the Rent Board Fee, and checking public Rent Increase License status.

short: SF Rent Board 2027 Informational Notice (Fee & Dec 14, 2026 Exemption Deadline)
title: Notification of Rent Board Fee and Housing Inventory Requirements (2027 Informational Notice)
quote: 2027 EXEMPTION WINDOW: Owner-occupied properties that are not rented at any time may be exempt from payment of the fee. ... Deadline to apply is Monday, December 14, 2026. Requesting a Rent Board Fee exemption does not satisfy Rent Board Housing Inventory reporting requirements. ... Reporting into the Rent Board Housing Inventory does not satisfy requesting an exemption of the Rent Board Fee.
used_for: Confirms the upcoming Monday, December 14, 2026 deadline to request a 2027 Rent Board Fee exemption (for an owner-occupied unit, if applicable) and the March 1, 2027 annual Housing Inventory deadline.

short: SF Rent Board Fee ($59.00/Unit for 2026–27)
title: The Rent Board Fee
quote: For the 2026-2027 tax year, the fee is: $59.00 per dwelling unit; $29.50 per guest unit ... Deadline: March 1 of each year for the Rent Board Fee. A 5% late penalty will be added to the amount of the fee every month following March 1 (for a maximum penalty of 15%). ... The deadline to submit a Request for Exemption for the 2027 Rent Board fee is December 14, 2026.
used_for: Distinguishes the annual $59.00/unit Rent Board Fee (and 5%/month late penalties up to 15%) from the free Housing Inventory / Rent Increase License.

short: SF Rent Board — Recover 50% ($29.50) of Fee from Tenant
title: Recover part of your Rent Board fee from the tenant
quote: A landlord who has paid the Rent Board fee in full may be able to collect 50% of the Rent Board fee (excluding any late penalties that have been added to the fee) from the tenant(s) residing in the unit. The landlord may only bill the tenant for the Rent Board fee if the tenant was residing in the unit on or before November 1 in the year before the fee became due. ... A tenant's failure to pay the Rent Board fee is not a just cause for eviction.
used_for: Prevents unlawful base-rent contamination: the 50% ($29.50) fee recovery must be deducted from security deposit interest or billed separately (30-day bill), never rolled into base rent.

short: SF Treasurer — Lessor of Residential Real Estate (<4 Units Carve-Out)
title: Information for Lessors of Residential Real Estate
publisher: San Francisco Office of the Treasurer & Tax Collector (sftreasurer.org)
quote: A person receiving rental income in connection with the operation of a cooperative housing corporation ... ; one residential structure consisting of fewer than four units; or one residential condominium is not, by reason of that fact alone, required to obtain a business registration certificate. If the same person engages in other business activities or incurs payroll expense, a business registration certificate may be required. Earning income from a short-term residential rental, regardless of the amount, is considered a business, therefore, you are required to register as a business.
used_for: Answers the second City registration question: an individual owner whose sole SF business activity is long-term rental of one 2-unit residential structure is not, by that fact alone, required to obtain a Business Registration Certificate.

short: SF Treasurer — Register a Business
title: Register a Business — Who Needs to Register in San Francisco?
publisher: San Francisco Office of the Treasurer & Tax Collector (sftreasurer.org)
quote: Unless otherwise required, you do not need to register if your only business is the receipt of rental income in connection with the operation of any of the following: 1. A cooperative housing corporation ... 2. One residential structure consisting of fewer than four units; or 3. One residential condominium.
used_for: Corroborates the <4-unit residential building carve-out from San Francisco Business Registration while identifying triggers (other SF business activity, payroll, >$500k gross receipts, short-term rentals) that override the exemption.

short: SF Rent Board Form 571 (1.6% for 3/1/26–2/28/27; Full 1982–2027 Schedule)
title: Form 571: Allowable Annual Rent Increases (2026–2027)
publisher: San Francisco Rent Board (sf.gov Official PDF)
used_for: Controlling official schedule for the current 1.6% annual rate and every historical banking rate period from April 1, 1982 through February 28, 2027.

short: SF Rent Board — Learn About Rent Increases (incl. Nov 9, 2026 Warning)
title: Learn about rent increases in San Francisco (Topic 050)
quote: The allowed rent increase percentage in San Francisco is 1.6%. The percentage is effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027. Notice: Proposed Changes to Rent Increase Limitations (Posted November 9, 2026): The San Francisco Board of Supervisors is considering legislation (File No. 261020) that would temporarily limit the combined amount of banked rent increases and capital improvement rent increases that may be imposed on rent-controlled units to 10% per year. If enacted as currently proposed, the legislation would apply to banked rent increases noticed on or after September 15, 2026 ... This legislation has not been enacted and is subject to change. ... Landlords must calculate the rent increase on the tenant's base rent only. ... Rent increases cannot be rounded up to the nearest dollar.
used_for: Establishes base-rent-only multiplication, ban on rounding up, 12-month anniversary rule, use of rate in force on the effective date, roommate surcharge prohibition, and the Nov 9, 2026 warning on File No. 261020.

short: SF Rent Board — Banked Rent Increases (incl. Nov 9, 2026 Warning)
title: Banked rent increases (Topic 503)
quote: A skipped increase is only banked if at least 24 full months pass without any rent increase. If less than 24 months pass, the skipped increase is lost and cannot be imposed at a later date. ... Partial increases: A landlord does not have to impose the maximum allowed increase. If only part of the allowable increase is used, the rest is banked. ... Banked increases do not have to be approved by the Rent Board, but must be calculated correctly. They cannot be compounded or prorated.
used_for: Governs 24-month no-increase banking phrasing, additive (non-compounded) percentage summation, partial-banking retention (used in Scenarios U2-C1 and U2-C2), and no Rent Board pre-approval for banked notices.

short: SF Admin. Code § 37.3 (Rent Limitations, Roommate Ban & Notice Breakdown)
title: Sec. 37.3 — Rent Limitations (S.F. Administrative Code Ch. 37)
quote: (a)(1) ... A landlord who has reported the required information about their rental unit to the Rent Board as set forth in Section 37.15 shall have a license to impose annually a rent increase which does not exceed a tenant's base rent by more than 60% of said published increase. In no event, however, shall the allowable annual increase be greater than 7%. (2) Banking ... (a)(11)(A) ... a landlord may not impose increases solely because a tenant has added an additional occupant to an existing tenancy ... notwithstanding a rental agreement or lease that specifically permits a rent increase for additional occupants. (b) Notice of Rent Increase for Tenants in Occupancy ... (b)(5) Nonconforming Rent Increases. Any rent increase which does not conform with the provisions of this section shall be null and void.
used_for: Primary enacted ordinance governing the 60%-of-CPI formula (7% ceiling), banking, additional-occupant surcharge ban, partial-occupancy bar (§ 37.3(d)(2)(B)), and written notice breakdown.

short: SF Rent Board Rules Part IV (§§ 4.10 Notice & 4.12 Banking)
title: Rent Board Rules and Regulations: Part IV — Rent Increases Not Requiring Approval by the Rent Board
quote: Section 4.10(b): Any rent increase which does not conform with the provisions of this Section shall render the entire rent increase null and void, unless the amount requested equals no more than the allowable annual and banked rent increase(s) ... Section 4.12(a): This banked amount may only be given at the time of an annual increase. ... A full 12 months must have elapsed from the date that an annual rent increase, or a portion thereof, could have been imposed before this banking section becomes applicable. Banked increases shall not be compounded and shall not be rounded up ... Section 4.12(b): In order to impose an accumulated rent increase the landlord shall: (1) inform the tenant, on or before the date upon which the landlord gives the tenant legal notice, which portion of the rent increase reflects banked amount, and (2) the dates upon which said banked amount is based; provided, however, that failure to include such information shall not render the increase null and void.
used_for: Supplies verbatim regulatory text for banking timing (with an annual increase, after 12 months from skipped availability), non-compounding/non-rounding, and the §§ 4.10(b)/4.12(b) non-voidness provisos.

short: SF BOS Legistar File #261020 (2026-11-11 Status: Pending Committee Action)
title: Board of Supervisors File No. 261020 — Administrative Code - Cap On Rent Increases for Rent-Controlled Units
quote: File #: 261020 Version: 1 | Name: Administrative Code - Cap On Rent Increases for Rent-Controlled Units | Type: Ordinance | Status: Pending Committee Action | Introduced: 9/15/2026 | In control: Land Use and Transportation Committee | On agenda: [blank] | Final action: [blank] | Enactment date: [blank].
used_for: Live 2026-11-11 verification that File No. 261020 has not been heard in committee, passed, or enacted, and remains Pending Committee Action.

short: SF BOS File #261020 Proposed Ordinance Text (Leg Ver1 — Proposed § 37.3(h))
title: File No. 261020 — Proposed Ordinance Text Version 1 (Leg Ver1)
quote: (h) Annual Limit for Rent Increases Under Sections 37.3(a)(2)-(3). A landlord may not impose banked rent increases under Section 37.3(a)(2), and/or rent increases based on any of the types of capital improvements described in Section 37.3(a)(3), that cause a tenant's rent to increase by more than a total of 10% of the lowest base rent that was in effect at any time during the 12 months immediately preceding the date the increase takes effect ... This 10% limit shall apply to banked rent increases based on rent increase notices provided on or after September 15, 2026 ... and shall remain in effect until December 31, 2029 unless extended by ordinance. A landlord may accumulate rent increases exceeding 10% per year during the time when this 10% limit is in effect, and may impose such increases to take effect on or after January 1, 2030, as otherwise permitted by law.
used_for: Confirms exact proposed statutory text of § 37.3(h): caps banked + capital-improvement increases (excluding the 1.6% annual § 37.3(a)(1) allowance) at 10% of lowest 12-month base rent for notices on/after Sept 15, 2026, preserving excess for Jan 1, 2030+.

short: SF BOS File #261020 Official Legislative Digest (Leg Dig Ver1)
title: File No. 261020 — City Attorney Official Legislative Digest Version 1
publisher: San Francisco Board of Supervisors / City Attorney (sfgov.legistar.com)
quote: The ordinance would set a combined 10% cap on Banked Increases and Capital Improvement Increases. Specifically, a landlord could not impose Banked Increases and/or Capital Improvement Increases that caused a tenant's rent to increase by more than 10% of the lowest base rent that was in effect during the previous 12 months. The 10% cap would apply to Banked Increases based on rent increase notices that landlords provided to their tenants on or after September 15, 2026 ... and would remain in effect until December 31, 2029.
used_for: Corroborates the exact scope of proposed File #261020 and motivates Scenario U2-C1 (10.0% banked + 1.6% annual = 11.6%, retaining 1.5% banked).

short: SF Rent Board — Learn About SF Rental Laws (June 13, 1979 Coverage Cutoff)
title: Learn about San Francisco rental laws
quote: Many residential units built on or before June 13, 1979 have both rent control and eviction protection. ... If your unit was built before June 14, 1979, and is not used as a single family dwelling, it may have both: Rent control [and] Eviction protection.
used_for: Confirms baseline coverage for a 1940 two-unit residential building while listing statutory exemptions (substantial rehabilitation, condo/single-family Costa-Hawkins, government-regulated subsidies) that must be checked against parcel records.

short: SF Rent Board — Landlord Petitions & Passthroughs (Topic 301)
title: Landlord Petitions and Passthroughs
quote: For certain types of rent increases, landlords must file a petition at the Rent Board before serving the tenants with a notice of the increase. ... There are six types of rent increases that require the filing of a landlord petition. These are: Capital Improvement Passthrough; Operating and Maintenance Expense Increase; Special Circumstances Increase Based on Rents for Comparable Units; Rent Increase Based on the Past Rent History of a Proposition I Affected Unit; Utility Passthrough (requires the filing of either a petition or a worksheet); and Rules and Regulations Section 1.21 Increase ... In addition, a landlord may elect to file a petition for a Rent Board determination of the tenant's current lawful rent.
used_for: Defines which rent-increase justifications require prior Rent Board petitions (O&M, Capital Improvements, Comparable Rents) versus petition-free annual/banked CPI increases, and notes optional Form 544 Lawful Rent Determination petitions.

short: SF Rent Board — Section 6.14 & Costa-Hawkins Overview (Topic 153)
title: Rent Increases Under Section 6.14 And Costa-Hawkins
quote: Rules and Regulations Section 6.14 provides for an unlimited rent increase on remaining occupants when the last original occupant vacates the unit, as long as the landlord timely served all remaining occupants with a written '6.14 notice.' ... Generally, sixty days is considered reasonable. ... Costa-Hawkins provides that when the last original occupant no longer permanently resides in the unit, the landlord may impose an unlimited rent increase on a lawful subtenant or assignee who did not reside in the unit prior to January 1, 1996. ... In addition, a co-tenant, as opposed to a subtenant, is not subject to such a rent increase, regardless of when the co-tenant moved in.
used_for: Explains why Unit 1 cannot be reset to market rate while Placeholder Tenant 1A (original Feb 1, 2025 occupant) remains, and distinguishes co-tenant vs. subtenant consequences for Placeholder Tenant 1D.

short: SF Rent Board Rules Part VI (§§ 6.10 O&M, 6.13 Roommate Ban, 6.14, 6.15A/B)
title: Rent Board Rules and Regulations: Part VI — Rent Increase Justifications
quote: Section 6.13: No extra rent may be charged solely for an additional occupant to an existing tenancy (including a newborn child), regardless of the presence of a rental agreement or lease which specifically allows for a rent increase for additional tenants. Section 6.14(b): Failure to give such a notice within 60 days of the landlord's actual knowledge of the occupancy by the subsequent occupant(s) establishes a rebuttable presumption that notice was not given within a reasonable period of time. Section 6.14(c): ... unless the subsequent occupant proves that the landlord waived his or her right to increase the rent by ... Failing, within 90 days of receipt of written notice ... to serve written notice of a rent increase or a reservation of the right ...
used_for: Provides exact regulatory rules for § 6.10 O&M petitions (7% max above annual; post-April 3, 2018 debt-service/property-tax exclusion), § 6.13 roommate surcharge ban, and § 6.14(b)/(c) 60-day vs. 90-day timelines.

short: SF Rent Board — Petition for Determination Under § 6.14 / Costa-Hawkins (Topic 329)
title: Petition for a Determination Pursuant to Section 6.14 and/or Costa-Hawkins
quote: Section 6.14 requires the last original occupant to 'vacate' the unit, while Costa-Hawkins only requires the last original occupant to no longer 'permanently reside' in the unit. A landlord is not required to file a petition with the Rent Board for approval of a rent increase pursuant to Section 6.14 or Costa-Hawkins Section 1954.53(d). However, if a landlord is unsure whether a rent increase is justified, the landlord may file a petition [Form 537] at the Rent Board.
used_for: Documents optional Rent Board determination petitions (Form 537) if the remaining original occupant in Unit 1 ever vacates in the future.

short: Cal. Civ. Code § 827 (30-Day vs. 90-Day Written Notice & Service Methods)
title: California Civil Code Section 827 — Change in Terms of Residential Tenancy
quote: (b)(1) ... the landlord may increase the rent provided in the lease or rental agreement, upon giving written notice to the tenant, as follows, by either of the following procedures: (A) By delivering a copy to the tenant personally. (B) By serving a copy by mail under the procedures prescribed in Section 1013 of the Code of Civil Procedure. (2) If the proposed rent increase for that tenant is 10 percent or less ... the notice shall be delivered at least 30 days before the effective date ... (3)(A) If the proposed rent increase ... is greater than 10 percent ... the notice shall be delivered at least 90 days before the effective date ...
used_for: Governs mandatory written delivery methods (personal delivery or CCP § 1013 mail only) and the 10.0% statutory threshold separating 30-day notice from 90-day notice.

short: Cal. CCP § 1013(a) (+5 Calendar Days for California Mail; +10/+20 Out-of-State/Country)
title: California Code of Civil Procedure Section 1013 — Service by Mail
quote: (a) Service is complete at the time of the deposit, but any period of notice ... shall be extended five calendar days, upon service by mail, if the place of address and the place of mailing is within the State of California, 10 calendar days if either the place of mailing or the place of address is outside the State of California but within the United States ... and 20 calendar days if either the place of mailing or the place of address is outside the United States.
used_for: Extends mail service lead times to 35 days (<=10% within CA) or 95 days (>10% within CA), and +10 / +20 days if mailed from outside California or outside the United States.

short: California Tenants Guide (Fixed-Term Lease Bar on Mid-Term Increases)
title: California Tenants — A Guide to Residential Tenants' and Landlords' Rights and Responsibilities (Rev. 2022)
publisher: California Department of Real Estate / California Courts (www4.courts.ca.gov)
quote: Fixed-term tenancies are tenancies that last for a set amount of time and have a defined expiration date, such as six months or one year. ... There are some advantages to having a fixed-term tenancy. For instance, the landlord cannot raise the tenant's rent during the tenancy, unless the rental agreement expressly allows rent increases.
used_for: Establishes the Unit 1 contract gate: if the April 1, 2026 occupancy agreement created a new 12-month fixed term without an escalation clause, no increase can take effect during that fixed term.

short: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12 (AB 1482 State Cap Yields to Stricter SF Rent Control)
title: California Civil Code Section 1947.12 — Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (AB 1482)
quote: (a)(1) ... an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower ... (d) This section shall not apply to the following residential real properties: ... (3) Housing subject to rent or price control through a public entity's valid exercise of its police power consistent with Chapter 2.7 (commencing with Section 1954.50) that restricts annual increases in the rental rate to an amount less than that provided in subdivision (a).
used_for: Proves California's statewide AB 1482 rent cap does not override or replace San Francisco's stricter 1.6% annual cap on covered 1940 rent-controlled units.

short: SF Rent Board — AB 1482 Report (8.8% Cap Inapplicable to SF Rent Ordinance Units)
title: The California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (AB 1482)
quote: The maximum rent increase for units under AB 1482 from August 1, 2026 to July 31, 2027 is 8.8% in San Francisco. This does NOT apply for units under the rent increase limitations of the San Francisco Rent Ordinance.
used_for: Prevents a common landlord error: using California's 8.8% AB 1482 figure on a pre-1979 SF Rent Ordinance unit is unlawful.

short: Cal. Civ. Code § 1954.53 (Costa-Hawkins Vacancy & Partial-Occupancy Rules)
title: California Civil Code Section 1954.53 — Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act
quote: (a) Notwithstanding any other provision of law, an owner of residential real property may establish the initial rental rate for a dwelling or unit ... (d)(2) If the original occupant or occupants who took possession of the dwelling or unit pursuant to the rental agreement with the owner no longer permanently reside there, an owner may increase the rent by any amount allowed by this section to a lawful sublessee or assignee who did not reside at the dwelling or unit prior to January 1, 1996. (d)(3) This subdivision does not apply to partial changes in occupancy of a dwelling or unit where one or more of the occupants of the premises, pursuant to the agreement with the owner provided for above, remains an occupant in lawful possession ...
used_for: Confirms initial vacancy decontrol at lease start and bars market resets on partial roommate turnover in Unit 1 while an original occupant remains.

short: Cal. Civ. Code § 1942.4 (35-Day Unabated Housing Citation Bar & Attorney's Fees)
title: California Civil Code Section 1942.4 — Substandard Dwelling Rent Increase Prohibition
quote: (a) A landlord of a dwelling may not demand rent, collect rent, issue a notice of a rent increase, or issue a three-day notice to pay rent or quit ... if all of the following conditions exist prior to the landlord's demand or notice: ... (2) A public officer or employee ... has notified the landlord or the landlord's agent in writing of his or her obligations to abate the nuisance or repair the substandard conditions. (3) The conditions have existed and have not been abated 35 days beyond the date of service ... without good cause. (b)(1) ... special damages of not less than one hundred dollars ($100) and not more than five thousand dollars ($5,000). (2) The prevailing party shall be entitled to recovery of reasonable attorney's fees and costs ...
used_for: Hard statutory red-team check: bars serving any rent increase notice when a DBI/DPH habitability citation has remained unabated >35 days without good cause.

short: SF Rent Board — Failure to Repair & Maintain Petitions (Topic 353, 60-Day Filing Window)
title: Failure to Repair and Maintain Petitions (Form 516B)
quote: A tenant may petition for a deferral of the annual rent increase if the landlord has failed to perform requested repairs, replacement or maintenance as required by state and/or local law. ... If the petition is granted, the proposed rent increase will be deferred or postponed until the requested repairs are made. ... The petition must be filed no later than 60 days following the tenant's receipt of the rent increase notice. ... The petition will not be granted if the repairs were completed before the effective date of the rent increase.
used_for: Shows how a tenant lawyer can defer an otherwise accurate 1.6% annual increase if requested habitability repairs remain incomplete on the effective date.

short: SF Rent Board — Tenant Financial Hardship Applications (Topic 363)
title: Tenant Financial Hardship Applications
quote: A tenant may seek relief from payment of the following types of rent increases or passthroughs on the grounds of financial hardship by filing a Tenant Financial Hardship Application with the Board: Capital Improvement Passthrough; Water Revenue Bond Passthrough; General Obligations Bond Passthrough; Utility Passthrough; Operating and Maintenance Expense Rent Increase. For all other types of rent increases or passthroughs, including annual and banked rent increases or rent increases authorized by the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act, financial hardship relief is not available.
used_for: Confirms that Rent Board financial hardship deferral applies to passthroughs/O&M petitions, not to annual or banked CPI increases.

short: Cal. Civ. Code § 1942.5 (180-Day Anti-Retaliation Statute)
title: California Civil Code Section 1942.5 — Retaliatory Conduct Prohibited
quote: (a) If the lessor retaliates against the lessee because of the exercise by the lessee of the lessee's rights under this chapter or because of the lessee's complaint to an appropriate agency as to tenantability of a dwelling, and if the lessee of a dwelling is not in default as to the payment of rent, the lessor may not ... increase the rent, or decrease any services within 180 days of any of the following ... (d) ... it is unlawful for a lessor to increase rent ... for the purpose of retaliating against the lessee because the lessee has lawfully organized or participated in a lessees' association ... or has lawfully and peaceably exercised any rights under the law. (f) This section does not limit in any way ... the lessor's right to do any of the acts described in subdivision (a) or (d) for any lawful cause.
used_for: Governs the 180-day retaliation screen after repair complaints/inspections and general anti-retaliation scrutiny when raising rent on one unit versus both units.

short: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955 (FEHA Housing Discrimination) & Cal. Civ. Code § 51 (Unruh)
title: California Government Code Section 12955 — Fair Employment and Housing Act
quote: (a) For the owner of any housing accommodation to discriminate against or harass any person because of the race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information of that person. (d) For any person subject to the provisions of Section 51 of the Civil Code [Unruh Civil Rights Act] ... to discriminate against any person ...
used_for: Primary California fair-housing prohibition governing selective vs. uniform rent increases; applies to a 2-unit rental property with no 'Mrs. Murphy' multi-unit exemption.

short: Cal. Civ. Code § 51 (Unruh Civil Rights Act)
title: California Civil Code Section 51 — Unruh Civil Rights Act
quote: (b) All persons within the jurisdiction of this state are free and equal, and no matter what their sex, race, color, religion, ancestry, national origin, disability, medical condition, genetic information, marital status, sexual orientation, citizenship, primary language, or immigration status are entitled to the full and equal accommodations, advantages, facilities, privileges, or services in all business establishments of every kind whatsoever.
used_for: Bars arbitrary and protected-characteristic discrimination (including age, citizenship, primary language, and immigration status) in California residential rentals.

short: 42 U.S.C. §§ 3604 & 3603 (Federal Fair Housing Act — GPO Official U.S. Code)
title: 42 U.S.C. § 3604 — Discrimination in the Sale or Rental of Housing (with 42 U.S.C. § 3603 Exemptions)
quote: § 3604(b): To discriminate against any person in the terms, conditions, or privileges of sale or rental of a dwelling, or in the provision of services or facilities in connection therewith, because of race, color, religion, sex, familial status, or national origin. § 3604(f)(2): [handicap/disability]. (Note: 42 U.S.C. § 3603(b)(2) exempts 1–4 family dwellings from § 3604 other than § 3604(c) ONLY if the owner actually occupies one unit as a residence; California FEHA/Unruh and SF § 37.10B provide no such 2-unit exemption.)
used_for: Federal Fair Housing Act prohibition on discriminatory rental terms and increases.

short: SF Admin. Code § 37.10C (Algorithmic Pricing Devices Ban)
title: Sec. 37.10C — Use and Sale of Algorithmic Devices Prohibited
quote: Sec. 37.10C(b): It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device described in subdivision (a) when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in San Francisco. ... (d)(2) civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation [plus attorney's fees]; (d)(3) [501(c)(3)/501(c)(4) SF tenant-rights nonprofit enforcement standing, Ord. 169-25 eff. Oct. 6, 2025].
